title: Chicken Milanese with Tomato and Mozzarella
subtitle: Italian-American veal parmigiana made with chicken breast
excerpt: Veal parmigiana is one of the defining dishes of Italian-American cooking: a breaded, fried cutlet topped with tomato sauce and melted mozzarella. This version uses chicken breast, which is both easier to source and gives a juicy result. The technique is the same.
sourceNotes: Veal parmigiana (veal Parmesan) is an Italian-American dish descended from the Sicilian melanzane alla parmigiana but adapted to use breaded and fried meat. Chicken breast is widely used as the accessible substitute. Note: veal is not in the master ingredient lookup; chicken breast is used here.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made up to three days ahead and refrigerated. Bread and fry the cutlets just before serving.

content.text: Chicken parmigiana is a breaded, pan-fried chicken breast finished in the oven under tomato sauce and melted mozzarella. It's the Italian-American version of a dish that started in Sicily as a vegetable preparation and became a meat dish in the United States. The keys are a thin, even cutlet and enough heat in the pan to colour the breadcrumb coat golden before the oven finishes the job.

items.prepNote: butterflied or pounded to 1 cm thickness

content.text: Heat {{olive-oil}} in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add {{garlic}} and cook for one minute until fragrant. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}}, season with salt, and simmer for 15 minutes until slightly thickened. Tear in half the {{basil}}. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C / gas mark 4). Butterfly the {{chicken-breast}} cutlets or place between two sheets of cling film and pound with a rolling pin to a uniform 1 cm thickness.

Set up three shallow dishes: one with seasoned {{plain-flour}}, one with beaten {{eggs}}, one with {{breadcrumbs-panko}} mixed with {{parmesan}} and {{italian-seasoning}}. Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg, then press firmly into the breadcrumb mixture on both sides.
Heat {{olive-oil}} in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets for three minutes per side until golden. Work in batches if needed: don't crowd the pan. Transfer to a baking tray.

Spoon two tablespoons of tomato sauce over each cutlet. Top with torn {{mozzarella}} and a little extra {{parmesan}}. Bake at 180°C for eight to ten minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Finish with the remaining {{basil}}.

items.symptom: The breadcrumbs fall off during frying
items.cause: Egg coating too thin, or oil not hot enough.
items.fix: Make sure each cutlet is pressed firmly into the breadcrumbs. The oil needs to be shimmering before the first cutlet goes in: test with a single breadcrumb, which should sizzle immediately.

items.symptom: The cutlet is dry and overcooked
items.cause: Chicken breast dries out quickly, especially if it's thick.
items.fix: Pound the cutlets to a true 1 cm thickness. The total cooking time from frying to oven should be about 12 to 14 minutes for a 1 cm cutlet.

items.symptom: The cheese hasn't melted and browned in ten minutes
items.cause: Oven temperature too low, or cheese applied from cold.
items.fix: Take the mozzarella out of the fridge 20 minutes before using. If the cheese still looks pale, switch on the grill for two to three minutes to finish.

items.symptom: The sauce makes the breadcrumbs soggy
items.cause: Too much sauce applied, or sauce too liquid.
items.fix: Use only two tablespoons of sauce per cutlet and spread it to within 1 cm of the edge. The sauce and cheese should sit on top of the crust, not soak through it.

content.text: Veal parmigiana is a signature Italian-American dish, developed by Sicilian and southern Italian immigrants in New York and New Jersey in the early 20th century. The model is the Sicilian melanzane alla parmigiana. In America the meat version became dominant. Chicken replaced veal in most homes by the second half of the 20th century. Serve over spaghetti or with a green salad.
